subject.title: [Feature]: Add tools.web.fetch.allowPrivateNetwork to allow private network access

question: Should OpenClaw expose broad private-network access for arbitrary `web_fetch` URLs, and if so should the public API be a nested/per-agent `ssrfPolicy.dangerouslyAllowPrivateNetwork` style policy rather than the requested top-level `allowPrivateNetwork` key?
rationale: The source shows the implementation primitive exists, but exposing it changes the SSRF boundary and current maintainer discussion has not settled the final public contract.

options.title: Approve nested audited policy
options.body: Land a default-off nested or per-agent SSRF policy with explicit dangerous naming, audit warnings, docs, cache separation, and redirect/metadata tests.

options.title: Approve global broad opt-in
options.body: Expose a simpler global private-network toggle and accept the larger blast radius with clear docs and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Reject broad private access
options.body: Keep arbitrary `web_fetch` strict and direct users to trusted proxies, narrow fake-IP flags, or purpose-built internal-service tools.

recommendation.title: Approve nested audited policy
recommendation.body: Land a default-off nested or per-agent SSRF policy with explicit dangerous naming, audit warnings, docs, cache separation, and redirect/metadata tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest visible combination of recent SSRF/web_fetch history and prior maintainer-context review on the rejected top-level shape.
